newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NUM, Northam close to agreement - union.
newsitem.headline: NUM, Northam close to agreement - union.

text.p: South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) and Northam Platinum Mines Ltd management were close to averting a strike after management made concessions on a minimum wage, a union official said on Monday.
Some 96.8 percent of NUM's 3,300 members at Northam voted in favour of strike action last Wednesday but talks have now brought the two sides close to agreement.
"We have made a lot of progress. We are just close to agreeing," NUM regional coordinator Mahlakeng Mahlakeng told Reuters by telephone from Rustenburg.
But he added a final decision had yet to be sealed. "We are unable, however, to confirm if we have called a strike off or if we are still going on strike," he said.

The union and management at the mine, owned by Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, reached deadlock over wage increases on September 26. The union had initially demanded a 15 percent pay hike but was prepared to accept management's offer of 10 percent.
NUM said the point of contention was wage parity, as Northam's minimum wage of around 556 rand was well below that of other mines.
But Mahlakeng said management had conceded points on the minimum wage issue. "There has been a movement on the part of management," he said
He added a final decision on whether or not a settlement had been agreed was due around 1900 (1700 GMT).
